Text: One Night
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: Never did the sun go down with a brighter glory on the quiet corner in
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: Soho, than one memorable evening when the Doctor and his daughter sat
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: under the plane-tree together. Never did the moon rise with a milder
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: radiance over great London, than on that night when it found them still
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: seated under the tree, and shone upon their faces through its leaves.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: Lucie was to be married to-morrow. She had reserved this last evening
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: for her father, and they sat alone under the plane-tree.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: “You are happy, my dear father?”
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: They had said little, though they had been there a long time. When it
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: in her usual work, nor had she read to him. She had employed herself in
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: both ways, at his side under the tree, many and many a time; but, this
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: time was not quite like any other, and nothing could make it so.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: upon his breast. In the moonlight which is always sad, as the light of

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: countenances which had been glaring at the prisoner a moment before, as
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: if with impatience to pluck him out into the streets and kill him.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: On these few steps of his dangerous way, Charles Darnay had set his foot
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: according to Doctor Manette’s reiterated instructions. The same cautious
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: counsel directed every step that lay before him, and had prepared every
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: inch of his road.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: The President asked, why had he returned to France when he did, and not
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: sooner?
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: He had not returned sooner, he replied, simply because he had no means
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: of living in France, save those he had resigned; whereas, in England,
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: he lived by giving instruction in the French language and literature.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: He had returned when he did, on the pressing and written entreaty of
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: a French citizen, who represented that his life was endangered by his
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: absence. He had come back, to save a citizen’s life, and to bear his
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: testimony, at whatever personal hazard, to the truth. Was that criminal
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: in the eyes of the Republic?
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: The populace cried enthusiastically, “No!” and the President rang his
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: bell to quiet them. Which it did not, for they continued to cry “No!”
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: until they left off, of their own will.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: The President required the name of that citizen. The accused explained
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: that the citizen was his first witness. He also referred with confidence
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: to the citizen’s letter, which had been taken from him at the Barrier,
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: but which he did not doubt would be found among the papers then before
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: the President.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: The Doctor had taken care that it should be there--had assured him that
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: it would be there--and at this stage of the proceedings it was produced
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: and read. Citizen Gabelle was called to confirm it, and did so. Citizen
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: Gabelle hinted, with infinite delicacy and politeness, that in the
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: pressure of business imposed on the Tribunal by the multitude of
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: enemies of the Republic with which it had to deal, he had been slightly
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: overlooked in his prison of the Abbaye--in fact, had rather passed out
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: of the Tribunal’s patriotic remembrance--until three days ago; when he
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: had been summoned before it, and had been set at liberty on the Jury’s
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: declaring themselves satisfied that the accusation against him was
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: answered, as to himself, by the surrender of the citizen Evrémonde,
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: called Darnay.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: Doctor Manette was next questioned. His high personal popularity,
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: and the clearness of his answers, made a great impression; but, as he
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: proceeded, as he showed that the Accused was his first friend on his
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: release from his long imprisonment; that, the accused had remained in
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: England, always faithful and devoted to his daughter and himself in
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: their exile; that, so far from being in favour with the Aristocrat
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: government there, he had actually been tried for his life by it, as
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: the foe of England and friend of the United States--as he brought these
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: circumstances into view, with the greatest discretion and with the
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: straightforward force of truth and earnestness, the Jury and the
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: populace became one. At last, when he appealed by name to Monsieur
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: Lorry, an English gentleman then and there present, who, like himself,
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: had been a witness on that English trial and could corroborate his
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: account of it, the Jury declared that they had heard enough, and that
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: they were ready with their votes if the President were content to
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: receive them.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: At every vote (the Jurymen voted aloud and individually), the populace
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: set up a shout of applause. All the voices were in the prisoner’s
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: favour, and the President declared him free.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: Then, began one of those extraordinary scenes with which the populace
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: sometimes gratified their fickleness, or their better impulses towards
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: generosity and mercy, or which they regarded as some set-off against
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: their swollen account of cruel rage. No man can decide now to which of
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: these motives such extraordinary scenes were referable; it is probable,
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: to a blending of all the three, with the second predominating. No sooner
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: was the acquittal pronounced, than tears were shed as freely as blood
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: at another time, and such fraternal embraces were bestowed upon the
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: prisoner by as many of both sexes as could rush at him, that after
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: his long and unwholesome confinement he was in danger of fainting from
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: exhaustion; none the less because he knew very well, that the very same
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: people, carried by another current, would have rushed at him with
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: the very same intensity, to rend him to pieces and strew him over the
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: streets.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: His removal, to make way for other accused persons who were to be tried,
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: rescued him from these caresses for the moment. Five were to be tried
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: together, next, as enemies of the Republic, forasmuch as they had not
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: assisted it by word or deed. So quick was the Tribunal to compensate
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: itself and the nation for a chance lost, that these five came down to
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: him before he left the place, condemned to die within twenty-four
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: hours. The first of them told him so, with the customary prison sign
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: of Death--a raised finger--and they all added in words, “Long live the
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: Republic!”
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: The five had had, it is true, no audience to lengthen their proceedings,
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: for when he and Doctor Manette emerged from the gate, there was a great
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: crowd about it, in which there seemed to be every face he had seen in
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: Court--except two, for which he looked in vain. On his coming out, the
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: concourse made at him anew, weeping, embracing, and shouting, all by
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: turns and all together, until the very tide of the river on the bank of
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: which the mad scene was acted, seemed to run mad, like the people on the
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: shore.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: They put him into a great chair they had among them, and which they had
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: taken either out of the Court itself, or one of its rooms or passages.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: Over the chair they had thrown a red flag, and to the back of it they
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: had bound a pike with a red cap on its top. In this car of triumph, not
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: even the Doctor’s entreaties could prevent his being carried to his home
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: on men’s shoulders, with a confused sea of red caps heaving about him,
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: and casting up to sight from the stormy deep such wrecks of faces, that
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: he more than once misdoubted his mind being in confusion, and that he
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: was in the tumbril on his way to the Guillotine.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: In wild dreamlike procession, embracing whom they met and pointing
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: him out, they carried him on. Reddening the snowy streets with the
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: prevailing Republican colour, in winding and tramping through them, as
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: they had reddened them below the snow with a deeper dye, they carried
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: him thus into the courtyard of the building where he lived. Her father
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: had gone on before, to prepare her, and when her husband stood upon his
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: feet, she dropped insensible in his arms.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: As he held her to his heart and turned her beautiful head between his
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: face and the brawling crowd, so that his tears and her lips might come
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: together unseen, a few of the people fell to dancing. Instantly, all the
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: rest fell to dancing, and the courtyard overflowed with the Carmagnole.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: Then, they elevated into the vacant chair a young woman from the
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: crowd to be carried as the Goddess of Liberty, and then swelling and
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: overflowing out into the adjacent streets, and along the river’s bank,
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: and over the bridge, the Carmagnole absorbed them every one and whirled
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: them away.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: After grasping the Doctor’s hand, as he stood victorious and proud
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: before him; after grasping the hand of Mr. Lorry, who came panting in
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: breathless from his struggle against the waterspout of the Carmagnole;
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: after kissing little Lucie, who was lifted up to clasp her arms round
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: his neck; and after embracing the ever zealous and faithful Pross who
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: lifted her; he took his wife in his arms, and carried her up to their
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: rooms.
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: “Lucie! My own! I am safe.”
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: “O dearest Charles, let me thank God for this on my knees as I have
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: prayed to Him.”
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: They all reverently bowed their heads and hearts. When she was again in
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: his arms, he said to her:
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: “And now speak to your father, dearest. No other man in all this France
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: could have done what he has done for me.”
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: She laid her head upon her father’s breast, as she had laid his poor
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: head on her own breast, long, long ago. He was happy in the return he
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: had made her, he was recompensed for his suffering, he was proud of his
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: strength. “You must not be weak, my darling,” he remonstrated; “don’t
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: tremble so. I have saved him.”
Title: A Tale of Two Cities

Text: Chapter XIV.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: It is a most miserable thing to feel ashamed of home. There may be
Title: Great Expectations

Text: black ingratitude in the thing, and the punishment may be retributive
Title: Great Expectations

Text: and well deserved; but that it is a miserable thing, I can testify.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: Home had never been a very pleasant place to me, because of my sister’s
Title: Great Expectations

Text: temper. But, Joe had sanctified it, and I had believed in it. I had
Title: Great Expectations

Text: believed in the best parlour as a most elegant saloon; I had believed
Title: Great Expectations

Text: in the front door, as a mysterious portal of the Temple of State whose
Title: Great Expectations

Text: solemn opening was attended with a sacrifice of roast fowls; I had
Title: Great Expectations

Text: believed in the kitchen as a chaste though not magnificent apartment; I
Title: Great Expectations

Text: had believed in the forge as the glowing road to manhood and
Title: Great Expectations

Text: independence. Within a single year all this was changed. Now it was all
Title: Great Expectations

Text: coarse and common, and I would not have had Miss Havisham and Estella
Title: Great Expectations

Text: see it on any account.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: How much of my ungracious condition of mind may have been my own fault,
Title: Great Expectations

Text: how much Miss Havisham’s, how much my sister’s, is now of no moment to
Title: Great Expectations

Text: me or to any one. The change was made in me; the thing was done. Well
Title: Great Expectations

Text: or ill done, excusably or inexcusably, it was done.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: Once, it had seemed to me that when I should at last roll up my
Title: Great Expectations

Text: shirt-sleeves and go into the forge, Joe’s ’prentice, I should be
Title: Great Expectations

Text: distinguished and happy. Now the reality was in my hold, I only felt
Title: Great Expectations

Text: that I was dusty with the dust of small-coal, and that I had a weight
Title: Great Expectations

Text: upon my daily remembrance to which the anvil was a feather. There have
Title: Great Expectations

Text: been occasions in my later life (I suppose as in most lives) when I
Title: Great Expectations

Text: have felt for a time as if a thick curtain had fallen on all its
Title: Great Expectations

Text: interest and romance, to shut me out from anything save dull endurance
Title: Great Expectations

Text: any more. Never has that curtain dropped so heavy and blank, as when my
Title: Great Expectations

Text: way in life lay stretched out straight before me through the newly
Title: Great Expectations

Text: entered road of apprenticeship to Joe.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: I remember that at a later period of my “time,” I used to stand about
Title: Great Expectations

Text: the churchyard on Sunday evenings when night was falling, comparing my
Title: Great Expectations

Text: own perspective with the windy marsh view, and making out some likeness
Title: Great Expectations

Text: between them by thinking how flat and low both were, and how on both
Title: Great Expectations

Text: there came an unknown way and a dark mist and then the sea. I was quite
Title: Great Expectations

Text: as dejected on the first working-day of my apprenticeship as in that
Title: Great Expectations

Text: after-time; but I am glad to know that I never breathed a murmur to Joe
Title: Great Expectations

Text: while my indentures lasted. It is about the only thing I _am_ glad to
Title: Great Expectations

Text: know of myself in that connection.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: For, though it includes what I proceed to add, all the merit of what I
Title: Great Expectations

Text: proceed to add was Joe’s. It was not because I was faithful, but
Title: Great Expectations

Text: because Joe was faithful, that I never ran away and went for a soldier
Title: Great Expectations

Text: or a sailor. It was not because I had a strong sense of the virtue of
Title: Great Expectations

Text: industry, but because Joe had a strong sense of the virtue of industry,
Title: Great Expectations

Text: that I worked with tolerable zeal against the grain. It is not possible
Title: Great Expectations

Text: to know how far the influence of any amiable honest-hearted duty-doing
Title: Great Expectations

Text: man flies out into the world; but it is very possible to know how it
Title: Great Expectations

Text: has touched one’s self in going by, and I know right well that any good
Title: Great Expectations

Text: that intermixed itself with my apprenticeship came of plain contented
Title: Great Expectations

Text: Joe, and not of restlessly aspiring discontented me.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: What I wanted, who can say? How can _I_ say, when I never knew? What I
Title: Great Expectations

Text: dreaded was, that in some unlucky hour I, being at my grimiest and
Title: Great Expectations

Text: commonest, should lift up my eyes and see Estella looking in at one of
Title: Great Expectations

Text: the wooden windows of the forge. I was haunted by the fear that she
Title: Great Expectations

Text: would, sooner or later, find me out, with a black face and hands, doing
Title: Great Expectations

Text: the coarsest part of my work, and would exult over me and despise me.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: Often after dark, when I was pulling the bellows for Joe, and we were
Title: Great Expectations

Text: singing Old Clem, and when the thought how we used to sing it at Miss
Title: Great Expectations

Text: Havisham’s would seem to show me Estella’s face in the fire, with her
Title: Great Expectations

Text: pretty hair fluttering in the wind and her eyes scorning me,—often at
Title: Great Expectations

Text: such a time I would look towards those panels of black night in the
Title: Great Expectations

Text: wall which the wooden windows then were, and would fancy that I saw her
Title: Great Expectations

Text: just drawing her face away, and would believe that she had come at
Title: Great Expectations

Text: last.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: After that, when we went in to supper, the place and the meal would
Title: Great Expectations

Text: have a more homely look than ever, and I would feel more ashamed of
Title: Great Expectations

Text: home than ever, in my own ungracious breast.

Text: Chapter XX.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: The journey from our town to the metropolis was a journey of about five
Title: Great Expectations

Text: hours. It was a little past midday when the four-horse stage-coach by
Title: Great Expectations

Text: which I was a passenger, got into the ravel of traffic frayed out about
Title: Great Expectations

Text: the Cross Keys, Wood Street, Cheapside, London.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: We Britons had at that time particularly settled that it was
Title: Great Expectations

Text: treasonable to doubt our having and our being the best of everything:
Title: Great Expectations

Text: otherwise, while I was scared by the immensity of London, I think I
Title: Great Expectations

Text: might have had some faint doubts whether it was not rather ugly,
Title: Great Expectations

Text: crooked, narrow, and dirty.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: Mr. Jaggers had duly sent me his address; it was, Little Britain, and
Title: Great Expectations

Text: he had written after it on his card, “just out of Smithfield, and close
Title: Great Expectations

Text: by the coach-office.” Nevertheless, a hackney-coachman, who seemed to
Title: Great Expectations

Text: have as many capes to his greasy great-coat as he was years old, packed
Title: Great Expectations

Text: me up in his coach and hemmed me in with a folding and jingling barrier
Title: Great Expectations

Text: of steps, as if he were going to take me fifty miles. His getting on
Title: Great Expectations

Text: his box, which I remember to have been decorated with an old
Title: Great Expectations

Text: weather-stained pea-green hammercloth moth-eaten into rags, was quite a
Title: Great Expectations

Text: work of time. It was a wonderful equipage, with six great coronets
Title: Great Expectations

Text: outside, and ragged things behind for I don’t know how many footmen to
Title: Great Expectations

Text: hold on by, and a harrow below them, to prevent amateur footmen from
Title: Great Expectations

Text: yielding to the temptation.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: I had scarcely had time to enjoy the coach and to think how like a
Title: Great Expectations

Text: straw-yard it was, and yet how like a rag-shop, and to wonder why the
Title: Great Expectations

Text: horses’ nose-bags were kept inside, when I observed the coachman
Title: Great Expectations

Text: beginning to get down, as if we were going to stop presently. And stop
Title: Great Expectations

Text: we presently did, in a gloomy street, at certain offices with an open
Title: Great Expectations

Text: door, whereon was painted MR. JAGGERS.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: “How much?” I asked the coachman.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: The coachman answered, “A shilling—unless you wish to make it more.”
Title: Great Expectations

Text: I naturally said I had no wish to make it more.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: “Then it must be a shilling,” observed the coachman. “I don’t want to
Title: Great Expectations

Text: get into trouble. _I_ know _him_!” He darkly closed an eye at Mr.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: Jaggers’s name, and shook his head.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: When he had got his shilling, and had in course of time completed the
Title: Great Expectations

Text: ascent to his box, and had got away (which appeared to relieve his
Title: Great Expectations

Text: mind), I went into the front office with my little portmanteau in my
Title: Great Expectations

Text: hand and asked, Was Mr. Jaggers at home?
Title: Great Expectations

Text: “He is not,” returned the clerk. “He is in Court at present. Am I
Title: Great Expectations

Text: addressing Mr. Pip?”
Title: Great Expectations

Text: I signified that he was addressing Mr. Pip.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: “Mr. Jaggers left word, would you wait in his room. He couldn’t say how
Title: Great Expectations

Text: long he might be, having a case on. But it stands to reason, his time
Title: Great Expectations

Text: being valuable, that he won’t be longer than he can help.”
Title: Great Expectations

Text: With those words, the clerk opened a door, and ushered me into an inner
Title: Great Expectations

Text: chamber at the back. Here, we found a gentleman with one eye, in a
Title: Great Expectations

Text: velveteen suit and knee-breeches, who wiped his nose with his sleeve on
Title: Great Expectations

Text: being interrupted in the perusal of the newspaper.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: “Go and wait outside, Mike,” said the clerk.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: I began to say that I hoped I was not interrupting, when the clerk
Title: Great Expectations

Text: shoved this gentleman out with as little ceremony as I ever saw used,
Title: Great Expectations

Text: and tossing his fur cap out after him, left me alone.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: Mr. Jaggers’s room was lighted by a skylight only, and was a most
Title: Great Expectations

Text: dismal place; the skylight, eccentrically pitched like a broken head,
Title: Great Expectations

Text: and the distorted adjoining houses looking as if they had twisted
Title: Great Expectations

Text: themselves to peep down at me through it. There were not so many papers
Title: Great Expectations

Text: about, as I should have expected to see; and there were some odd
Title: Great Expectations

Text: objects about, that I should not have expected to see,—such as an old
Title: Great Expectations

Text: rusty pistol, a sword in a scabbard, several strange-looking boxes and
Title: Great Expectations

Text: packages, and two dreadful casts on a shelf, of faces peculiarly
Title: Great Expectations

Text: swollen, and twitchy about the nose. Mr. Jaggers’s own high-backed
Title: Great Expectations

Text: chair was of deadly black horsehair, with rows of brass nails round it,
Title: Great Expectations

Text: like a coffin; and I fancied I could see how he leaned back in it, and
Title: Great Expectations

Text: bit his forefinger at the clients. The room was but small, and the
Title: Great Expectations

Text: clients seemed to have had a habit of backing up against the wall; the
Title: Great Expectations

Text: wall, especially opposite to Mr. Jaggers’s chair, being greasy with
Title: Great Expectations

Text: shoulders. I recalled, too, that the one-eyed gentleman had shuffled
Title: Great Expectations

Text: forth against the wall when I was the innocent cause of his being
Title: Great Expectations

Text: turned out.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: I sat down in the cliental chair placed over against Mr. Jaggers’s
Title: Great Expectations

Text: chair, and became fascinated by the dismal atmosphere of the place. I
Title: Great Expectations

Text: called to mind that the clerk had the same air of knowing something to
Title: Great Expectations

Text: everybody else’s disadvantage, as his master had. I wondered how many
Title: Great Expectations

Text: other clerks there were upstairs, and whether they all claimed to have
Title: Great Expectations

Text: the same detrimental mastery of their fellow-creatures. I wondered what
Title: Great Expectations

Text: was the history of all the odd litter about the room, and how it came
Title: Great Expectations

Text: there. I wondered whether the two swollen faces were of Mr. Jaggers’s
Title: Great Expectations

Text: family, and, if he were so unfortunate as to have had a pair of such
Title: Great Expectations

Text: ill-looking relations, why he stuck them on that dusty perch for the
Title: Great Expectations

Text: blacks and flies to settle on, instead of giving them a place at home.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: Of course I had no experience of a London summer day, and my spirits
Title: Great Expectations

Text: may have been oppressed by the hot exhausted air, and by the dust and
Title: Great Expectations

Text: grit that lay thick on everything. But I sat wondering and waiting in
Title: Great Expectations

Text: Mr. Jaggers’s close room, until I really could not bear the two casts
Title: Great Expectations

Text: on the shelf above Mr. Jaggers’s chair, and got up and went out.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: When I told the clerk that I would take a turn in the air while I
Title: Great Expectations

Text: waited, he advised me to go round the corner and I should come into
Title: Great Expectations

Text: Smithfield. So I came into Smithfield; and the shameful place, being
Title: Great Expectations

Text: all asmear with filth and fat and blood and foam, seemed to stick to
Title: Great Expectations

Text: me. So, I rubbed it off with all possible speed by turning into a
Title: Great Expectations

Text: street where I saw the great black dome of Saint Paul’s bulging at me
Title: Great Expectations

Text: from behind a grim stone building which a bystander said was Newgate
Title: Great Expectations

Text: Prison. Following the wall of the jail, I found the roadway covered
Title: Great Expectations

Text: with straw to deaden the noise of passing vehicles; and from this, and
Title: Great Expectations

Text: from the quantity of people standing about smelling strongly of spirits
Title: Great Expectations

Text: and beer, I inferred that the trials were on.
Title: Great Expectations

Text: While I looked about me here, an exceedingly dirty and partially drunk
Title: Great Expectations

Text: minister of justice asked me if I would like to step in and hear a
Title: Great Expectations

Text: trial or so: informing me that he could give me a front place for half
Title: Great Expectations

Text: a crown, whence I should command a full view of the Lord Chief Justice
Title: Great Expectations

Text: in his wig and robes,—mentioning that awful personage like waxwork, and
Title: Great Expectations

Text: presently offering him at the reduced price of eighteen-pence. As I
Title: Great Expectations

Text: declined the proposal on the plea of an appointment, he was so good as
Title: Great Expectations

Text: to take me into a yard and show me where the gallows was kept, and also
Title: Great Expectations

Text: where people were publicly whipped, and then he showed me the Debtors’
Title: Great Expectations

Text: Door, out of which culprits came to be hanged; heightening the interest
Title: Great Expectations

Text: of that dreadful portal by giving me to understand that “four on ’em”
Title: Great Expectations

Text: would come out at that door the day after to-morrow at eight in the
Title: Great Expectations

Text: morning, to be killed in a row. This was horrible, and gave me a
Title: Great Expectations
